newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court won't stop Hong Kong extradition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court won't stop Hong Kong extradition.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday refused to block the extradition to Hong Kong of Jerry Lui Kin-hong, who faces multimillion dollar bribery and conspiracy charges relating to cigarette smuggling.

He had asked the Supreme Court for a stay of a ruling by a federal appeals court in Boston ordering his extradition. Lui had wanted the appeals court ruling put on hold, pending the filing of an appeal with the nation's high court.

A federal judge in Boston earlier this year blocked Lui's extradition after his lawyers said he faced possible execution if forced to return to Hong Kong as his trial was unlikely to be completed before China takes control of the British colony on July 1.
But U.S. government lawyers appealed the judge's decision, and the appeals court ruled in their favour in March.
Lui's request for a stay was denied by a 7-2 vote, with only Justices Stephen Breyer and John Paul Stevens dissenting.
"In essence, (Lui) says that the United States intends to extradite him not to the United Kingdom or to a crown colony of the United Kingdom for trial, but rather to ... China," Breyer said.
Breyer said Lui raised questions about the "lawfulness" of the extradition, and added that he would grant a stay at least until the U.S. government files its response.
Lui was arrested at Boston's Logan International Airport when he flew there from Canada to visit a sick friend in December 1995.
